goalTree.description:
Two projects, adopted, and now to be integrated: linetokens is brought into cashbook. Each was written
  before, by someone else, and each already builds and passes its own tests. In their own words, from their
  READMEs:

    "cashbook -- An append-only ledger of entries in cents, per account: append, transfer between accounts,
    balances, the accounts in use."
    "linetokens -- Reads `name=value; name=value` lines into tokens: bare or quoted values, escapes inside
    quotes, and an error that says where in the line it went wrong."

  The build has two modules: linetokens/ is the linetokens project, cashbook/ is the cashbook project and
  depends on linetokens. The root pom.xml only lists the two modules. Both projects' tests are in their
  modules' src/test/java.

  The integration wanted, with the focus on import: the ledger imports entries from name=value lines, read
  with linetokens' LineTokenizer -- not with a second tokenizer.

  - LedgerImport.importLines(Ledger ledger, List<String> lines) appends one Entry per accepted line, in order,
    and returns an ImportReport.
  - ImportReport is a record of the number of lines imported (int imported) and the rejected lines
    (List<Rejection> rejected, in line order, a list that cannot be modified).
  - Rejection is a record of the line's number counting from 1 (int line), a position (int position) and a
    reason (String reason).
  - A blank line is skipped; lines are numbered as given, blank ones included.
  - A line is read with LineTokenizer.tokenize. A line it rejects is rejected with the TokenizeException's own
    position and message.
  - The names are account, amount and memo. account and amount are required; memo is optional (an Entry
    without one has the empty memo). Any other name rejects the line with "unknown name '<name>'".
  - amount is a decimal with at most two places and an optional leading '-' ("12.50" is 1250 cents, "-3" is
    -300, "0.5" is 50); one that is not, or is zero, rejects the line with "invalid amount".
  - A line without an account (or with a blank one) is rejected with "missing account", one without an amount
    with "missing amount". Rejections that do not come from the tokenizer have position -1.
  - A rejected line appends nothing and does not stop the import.

  The specification is LedgerImportSpecTest, LedgerSpecTest and LineTokensSpecTest in src/test/java: LedgerImportSpecTest says exactly what the integration must do and fails until
  the code provides it; the other two are each project's own specification and keep passing.

  OBJECTIVE: every test in LedgerImportSpecTest passes, and the whole suite passes.

  The classes to change are LedgerImport, ImportReport and Rejection -- none exists yet: create them under
  cashbook/src/main/java in package org.cashbook.ledger. DO NOT modify anything under linetokens/src/test and cashbook/src/test: the specifications and
  tests are the operators', and if one fails, the code is what is wrong. Keep every class either project
  already has exactly as it is.

subGoals.description:
A new project, adopted as it stands. Its tree holds only its build file (pom.xml), a README, and the
  operator's specification under src/test/java; nothing exists under src/main/java yet. In its own words,
  from its README:

    "cashbook -- An append-only ledger of entries in cents, per account: append, transfer between accounts,
    balances, the accounts in use."

  It is a library, in package org.cashbook.ledger, with no dependencies beyond the JDK.

  - Entry is a record of an account (String), an amount in cents (long, amountCents) and a memo (String).
    An entry needs an account that is not null or blank and an amount that is not zero, else it raises
    IllegalArgumentException; a null memo becomes the empty string.
  - Ledger is a class with a no-argument constructor; it starts empty.
  - append(Entry) adds the entry at the end and returns its number, counting from 1.
  - transfer(String from, String to, long cents, String memo) appends two entries with that memo: first
    from's debit (-cents), then to's credit (+cents), and returns the number of the credit. It raises
    IllegalArgumentException, appending nothing, when cents is not positive or from and to are the same.
  - entries() returns every entry in the order appended, as a List that cannot be modified and does not change
    when more are appended later.
  - balance(String account) returns the sum of that account's amounts as a long, 0 for an account with no entries.
  - accounts() returns the accounts that have entries, each once, in alphabetical order, as a List that cannot
    be modified.

  The specification is LedgerSpecTest in src/test/java: its tests say exactly what the ledger must return,
  and they fail until the code provides it.

  OBJECTIVE: every test in LedgerSpecTest passes, and the whole suite passes.

  The classes to change are Entry and Ledger -- neither exists yet: create them under src/main/java in package
  org.cashbook.ledger. DO NOT modify anything under src/test: the specification is the operator's, and if one
  of its tests fails, the code is what is wrong.

subGoals.description:
A new project, adopted as it stands. Its tree holds only its build file (pom.xml), a README, and the
  operator's specification under src/test/java; nothing exists under src/main/java yet. In its own words,
  from its README:

    "linetokens -- Reads `name=value; name=value` lines into tokens: bare or quoted values, escapes inside
    quotes, and an error that says where in the line it went wrong."

  It is a library, in package org.linekit.tokens, with no dependencies beyond the JDK.

  - Token is a record of a name and a value (both String).
  - LineTokenizer.tokenize(String line) returns the line's pairs as a List of Token, in line order; the list
    cannot be modified.
  - Pairs are separated by ';'. A separator at the very end of the line is allowed. An empty or blank line
    has no tokens.
  - A pair is name=value. Spaces around the name and around a bare value are not part of them.
  - A name starts with a letter and holds only letters, digits and underscores.
  - A bare value is everything up to the next ';' (it may be empty).
  - A quoted value starts with '"' (spaces before the quote are skipped) and ends at the next '"' that is not
    escaped. Inside it ';', '=' and spaces are part of the value; a backslash followed by '"' or by a
    backslash stands for that character. After the closing quote only spaces may come before the next ';'.
  - A line that breaks these rules raises TokenizeException, an IllegalArgumentException with a position()
    -- the 0-based index in the line where the problem is -- and a message that names it:
      a pair without '='                 -> "missing '='", at the pair's first character
      a name that is not a name          -> "invalid name", where the name starts (position 0 for "=x")
      a quote that is never closed       -> "unterminated quote", at the opening quote
      anything after a closing quote     -> "after closing quote", where that text starts
      a name already used in the line    -> "duplicate name", where the second one starts
  - TokenizeException has a constructor TokenizeException(String message, int position).

  The specification is LineTokensSpecTest in src/test/java: its tests say exactly what the library must
  return, and they fail until the code provides it.

  OBJECTIVE: every test in LineTokensSpecTest passes, and the whole suite passes.

  The classes to change are Token, TokenizeException and LineTokenizer -- none exists yet: create them under
  src/main/java in package org.linekit.tokens. DO NOT modify anything under src/test: the specification is
  the operator's, and if one of its tests fails, the code is what is wrong.

subGoals.description: Create LineTokenizer in package org.linekit.tokens under src/main/java with a static tokenize(String line) returning an unmodifiable List<Token> in line order, implementing all spec rules: ';' separation (trailing separator allowed), empty/blank line yields no tokens, name=value pairs with trimmed name and bare value, name validation (letter start; letters/digits/underscores), bare value up to next ';', quoted values (skip leading spaces, ';'/'='/spaces inside, backslash-escaped '"' and '\\', only spaces allowed before next ';'), and TokenizeException with the exact messages and 0-based positions for missing '=', invalid name, unterminated quote, after closing quote, and duplicate name.

acceptanceCriteria: Create LineTokenizer.java
Create TokenizeException.java
tokenize returns a list that cannot be modified (add/remove/set throw UnsupportedOperationException)
Pairs appear in line order with name and value trimmed of surrounding spaces for bare values
A trailing ';' and an empty/blank line produce an empty token list
A pair without '=' raises TokenizeException "missing '='" at the pair's first character
A non-name (e.g. "=x") raises TokenizeException "invalid name" at the name's start (position 0 for "=x")
An unclosed quote raises TokenizeException "unterminated quote" at the opening quote
Non-space text after a closing quote raises TokenizeException "after closing quote" at that text's start
A repeated name raises TokenizeException "duplicate name" at the second occurrence's start
Quoted values preserve ';', '=', and spaces, and backslash-escaped '"' and '\\' decode to the literal character
Every test in LineTokensSpecTest passes
